meta.description:
Say hello to the cutest squirrels of all time! OK, well, maybe not, but these Oregon ground squirrels are incredibly cute, and very curious. 
BLM crews were out inspecting the sagebrush habitat north of Jordan Valley on the Oregon-Idaho border when the Belding’s ground squirrels came out for a look.
About 20,000 acres of the area burned in 2012 in the Danner Loop II Fire. Since then it has been targeted for sagebrush planting to rehabilitate habitat. This includes plantings by inmates from the Snake River Correctional Institution. 
Video captured April 20, 2016, by Larry Morre, BLM

More public domain wildlife video clips and photographs on our Flickr album: www.flickr.com/photos/blmoregon/sets/72157629309711281

meta.artist: Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area
meta.description: In December of 2017, we captured this cute footage of P-42's two untagged kittens feeding on a deer, chirping for mom, and just generally being kittens. So far this is looking like a happier ending than P-42's litter from last year, which she abandoned. We hope to capture these animals when they are older and outfit them with a GPS collar so that we can learn more about their transition into adulthood and dispersal. Capturing them will also give us a chance to run their DNA and see how they may be related to other mountain lions in the area.

meta.artist: Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area
meta.credit: Five Kittens Born in Santa Susana Mountains
meta.description:
National Park Service researchers discovered two litters of mountain lion kittens in the eastern Santa Susana Mountains in June 2016. A total of five kittens, three females and two males, were eartagged and returned to their respective dens earlier this month. 
P-48 and P-49, both females, were born to P-35. 
P-50 (male), P-51 (female), and P-52 (male) were born to P-39. 

In both cases, P-38 is suspected to be the father.
